profile.headline: Founding Engineer | Full-Stack TypeScript & Python | React, React Native, Next.js, Node, Postgres | AI Integration | 5+ yrs solo-shipping production systems
profile.summary:
I'm a problem solver who builds software end-to-end.
For the last 5 years I've shipped production systems independently, most recently News Nexus, a 5-service platform delivering weekly news-clip reports under a US federal contract (Consumer Product Safety Commission via Kinetic Metrics), and the Kyber Vision volleyball-analytics mobile app for a European sports-tech product.
Before engineering, 15 years as an economist in Washington, DC. In April 2019, I ran my first Python script one Saturday morning — it took all my patience just to set up the environment. Today my skills (and my patience) have grown.
My experience includes:
✓ Full-stack TypeScript + Python in one platform
✓ React, React Native (Expo), Next.js, Redux Toolkit, Tailwind
✓ Node.js (Express 5), Python (FastAPI), REST API design, JWT auth
✓ Postgres + Sequelize at production scale, schema migration
✓ BullMQ + Redis queues, custom FIFO with cooperative cancellation
✓ AI integration (OpenAI, HuggingFace, semantic + dedupe scoring)
✓ Media pipelines (ffmpeg, YouTube API, Playwright scraping)
✓ DevOps on Ubuntu (reverse proxy, GitHub Actions CI)
✓ Solo ownership: architecture → build → ops → stakeholders
Allergic to scope creep and to engineering that doesn't ship. Open to founding-engineer and early-stage roles where breadth, ownership, and shipping matter more than specialization.
When I'm not coding: guitar, reading, French.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Building production software end-to-end and independently as Dashboards and Databases. Over 5 years I've shipped systems for paying clients, equity-stake partners, and personal products across full-stack web (TypeScript, Python, Node, Next.js), mobile (React Native), AI, and DevOps (Ubuntu, Redis/BullMQ).

Selected projects:

- Encipher Systems (https://enciphersystems.com/). Built and deployed the company website from a client Figma design: added custom animations, coded it from scratch, and shipped to the client's custom domain. Next.js 16 / React 19 with a hardened Nodemailer contact form.

- News Nexus (https://news-nexus-lite.dashanddata.com/). Sole builder and operator of a 5-service production platform for a US federal contract with the Consumer Product Safety Commission (via Kinetic Metrics). Ingests news from many sources into Postgres 16 via a Sequelize package, runs deduplication, semantic and location scoring, OpenAI state classification, and scraping through Node and Python workers, then serves a Next.js review portal for human clip approval and weekly PDF/Excel delivery.

- Tastermonial (https://tastermonial.com/). Personalized-nutrition app with many partners and over 10,000 users. Added Oura Ring support so users pair sleep, readiness, and recovery data with CGM glucose data. Built it in the Python/FastAPI backend: users connect Oura via Junction's hosted OAuth, which streams events to a webhook the service normalizes into Postgres sleep records.

- Go Lightly (https://go-lightly.love/). Guided-meditation platform where users compose meditations from ElevenLabs text-to-speech, sounds, and timed pauses. TypeScript monorepo: Next.js 16 web app, Express 5 API, and an ffmpeg job-queue worker over PostgreSQL.

- Kyber Vision (https://kybervision.eu/, equity stake). Built the Expo/React Native mobile app for a volleyball analysis platform: live match-event scripting via a custom court tap and swipe-wheel gesture system, plus video review and montages.
positions.insights: Skills: JavaScript · Mobile Applications · Python (Programming Language) · DevOps · Linux Server · Video Editing · Software Infrastructure · Software Design · Software Industry · Engineering · Web Engineering

positions.title: Economist
positions.description:
Eight years as a federal economist focused on supply-chain analytics, price-growth analysis, and vendor proposal evaluation. Built quantitative analyses on large datasets to answer questions about industry pricing, supply-chain vulnerabilities, and proposal cost realism. Methods and tools: regression analysis, uncertainty analysis, forecasting, Bureau of Labor Statistics price-index methodology, VBA (Excel automation), and SAS JMP scripting. Team lead on multiple engagements, with regular technical writing for non-technical decision-makers.

Selected projects:

- Ship construction price-growth negotiation (lead analyst). Built the Government's analytical position for a major proposal negotiation. For each part in the proposal, ran regressions against historical purchase records, mapped each part to an appropriate Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) price index using qualitative-similarity and growth-range checks, combined third-party BLS index forecasts into a Government-position forecast, and produced uncertainty bounds based on observed historical growth. Implemented in VBA and SAS JMP.

- NATO inflation history. Authored a 40-year history of US inflation, presented at a NATO conference. Covered drivers and policy context across the period.

- VBA tooling for external data ingest. Built Excel/VBA tools that automated extraction of data from external sources to feed the team's recurring analyses, replacing manual workflows.
positions.insights: Skills: Economic Indicators · Economic Statistics · Economic Analysis · Mathematical Economics

positions.title: Associate
positions.description:
Three years in ICF International's energy practice, delivering forecasting and analytics work for US electricity market clients including utilities, regional transmission organizations, and federal agencies. Methods and tools: linear programming models, econometric and regression modeling, large database management (model inputs sourced from ISOs/RTOs, electric companies, and data providers including Platt's and SNL), and client-facing analytical delivery.

Selected projects:

- US electricity market forecasting. Used ICF's proprietary linear-program model of US electricity markets to deliver power-plant valuations, energy-price forecasts, market-share forecasts, and other indicators for utility and RTO clients.

- NREL cross-model comparison study. Lead on database development and major contributor to the published analytical report comparing technology costs and performance parameters across seven energy market models: MARKAL, NEMS, GPRA, ReEDS, MERGE, MiniCAM, and EPA IPM.

- ARRA federal grants advisory. Advised regional governments on applying for American Recovery and Reinvestment Act funding for energy-efficiency infrastructure, including public-transit vehicles and building upgrades.

positions.title: Economist
positions.description:
Fourteen months at HDR | HLB Decision Economics doing economic and risk modeling for infrastructure clients across the US, spanning both public-sector evaluation work and private-sector market assessment. Methods and tools: cost-benefit analysis, cost and schedule risk modeling (Monte Carlo cost-risk methods), statistical and regression modeling for market sizing, and infrastructure-sector analysis across water, power, ports, rail, and aviation.

Selected projects:

- Southeastern US construction market assessment. For a large US contractor, assessed market potential across water/wastewater, power, seaports, rail, and airports sectors. Led areas of analysis involving risk and statistical modeling. Output shaped the client's resource-allocation strategy for project pursuit across the region.

- Transportation infrastructure project evaluations. Cost-benefit modeling for public-entity clients. Reports informed how these clients prioritized public funding awards across competing infrastructure projects.

- Cost and schedule risk modeling for infrastructure projects. Built Monte Carlo cost-risk analyses to estimate total cost and approximate schedule for projects under uncertainty, used by clients to size contingency and set baseline expectations.
positions.insights: Skills: Economic Indicators · Economic Analysis · Mathematical Economics · Economic Statistics

positions.title: Industry Economist
positions.description:
Two and a half years as an industry economist at the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), focused on the retail electricity industry. Methods and tools: survey-data methodology and edit-check design, energy-model interpretation, web data-product development, and analytical writing for industry and policy audiences. Served as a point of contact for external data and general industry inquiries.

Selected projects:

- Electricity sales and revenue survey. Developed and analyzed edit checks for the survey, improving data-collection efficiency and surfacing industry trends for analysis in EIA reports and publications.

- Office of Analysis and Integrated Forecasting (OAIF) detail. Summarized results of an energy model during a detail assignment focused on the economic effects of a potential new policy.

- EIA web data products. Developed, improved, and maintained EIA's web data products on retail electricity, working with IT staff to take products to production. Led projects.
